To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long-term ordering of impurities in a semiconductor crystal is a universal phenomenon that can be used to create new types of nanocrystals with improved properties and to design a new generation of semiconductor devices.

the luminescence of long-term ordered pure and doped GaP crystals is due to a high-density exciton bound to a nitrogen superlattice and that the luminescent properties of GaP:N and GaP:N:Er nanocrystals are due to the formation of a GaP:N, Er superlattice.
the luminescence of long-term ordered GaP:N crystals and GaP:N:Er, GaP:N, and GaP:N:Mg nanocrystals embedded in a transparent fluorine-containing polymer matrix is due to impurity ordering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of optoelectronics based on the use of long-term ordering of impurities in the semiconductor crystal lattice and the formation of new crystal structures.
the development of a new type and a new generation of semiconductor materials and devices.
the creation of novel luminescence materials and devices based on the formation of ordered crystal lattices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
long-term ordering is the most efficient and reliable method for the production of high-quality crystals.
the long-term ordering of impurities in the crystal lattice leads to the formation of a superlattice of the impurity and the crystal lattice.
long-term ordering is a new phenomenon in the physics of semiconductors and a new approach to the creation of a new class of optoelectronics devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a new type of ordered crystal lattice in which the impurity atoms form a superlattice that modifies and improves the properties of the crystal lattice.
the ordering phenomenon in GaP and other III–V crystals is a very promising and important area for research and applications.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to create a crystal lattice with a periodic structure of impurities, which can be used to create a new generation of semiconductor devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long-range ordering of the crystal lattice and impurities is the key to improving the luminescence properties of semiconductors.
the luminescence intensity and lifetime of long-term ordered GaP crystals are much higher than in disordered crystals.
the long-term ordered GaP crystals have the potential to be used as the building blocks for the new type of optoelectronics devices.
